# Contributing and developing

## Reporting issues

Report issues on the [Cabby issue tracker](https://github.com/MISP/cabby/issues).

## Obtaining the source code

Download or clone the [Cabby repository](https://github.com/MISP/cabby).

## Layout

The Cabby repository has the following layout:

- `docs/` contains the [documentation](https://misp.github.io/cabby/).
- `cabby/` contains the library and command-line tools.
- `tests/` contains the test suite.

## Develop with uv

Install uv as described in the [installation](installation.qmd) guide. From the repository
root, create a virtual environment and install Cabby in editable mode with its
development dependencies:

```sh
uv venv --python 3.12
uv pip install -r requirements-dev.txt -e .
```

Activate the environment before running the tests or CLI commands. In a POSIX
shell, run `. .venv/bin/activate`. In PowerShell, run
`.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`.

## Running the tests

From the activated environment, run:

```sh
python -m pytest --cov=cabby
python -m flake8
taxii-discovery --help
```

To run the existing tox environments, use `uvx --python 3.12 --with tox-uv tox -e py312,flake8`.

## Generating the documentation

The site uses the [MISP book](https://github.com/MISP/misp-book) template.
Install [Quarto 1.9.38](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/), uv, and Make. Then
run the following from the repository root. The docs extra provides autodoc,
which generates the API chapter from Cabby's Python docstrings.

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --extra docs make -C docs html
```

Open `docs/_book/index.html` to browse the result, or use
`uv run --python 3.12 --extra docs make -C docs preview` while editing.

The Documentation workflow checks the site on pull requests and publishes it
to [GitHub Pages](https://misp.github.io/cabby/) on pushes to `master`. For
the initial setup, select **GitHub Actions** as the publishing source under
**Settings → Pages → Build and deployment**. To redeploy, run the workflow
manually from `master`.

## Publish a release to PyPI

Before the first release, a PyPI maintainer must register a GitHub pending
publisher on the [PyPI publishing page](https://pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/).
If the project already exists, use its **Publishing** settings. Enter these
values so PyPI can identify the release job.

| PyPI field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| PyPI project name | `misp-cabby` |
| Owner | `MISP` |
| Repository name | `cabby` |
| Workflow filename | `publish.yml` |
| Environment name | `pypi` |

1. Set the new version in `cabby/_version.py`, update `CHANGES.md`, and merge
   those changes into `master`.
2. Publish a [GitHub Release](https://github.com/MISP/cabby/releases/new)
   for that commit. Use the package version as the tag, for example `0.1.24`.
3. Check the **Publish to PyPI** workflow. It builds and validates the wheel
   and source distribution, checks the tag against the built version, and
   uses the `pypi` environment to obtain a short-lived publishing token.
   Both files appear on the [misp-cabby project page](https://pypi.org/project/misp-cabby/).
